title: Lake County Commission, District 2
what_it_does: County commissioners set the county budget and property-tax (millage) rate, adopt land-use and zoning rules, and oversee county services such as roads, parks, libraries, fire/EMS and utilities.
verified_ballot_note: Only the incumbent's candidacy was confirmed in snippets (Yahoo/Daily Commercial preview). Whether he faces a November opponent could not be verified; check https://www.lakevotes.gov/190/Current-County-Candidates-Committees.

candidates.name: Sean M. Parks
candidates.occupation: Lake County commissioner since 2010; certified planner with environmental-science and engineering-management degrees
candidates.background: Sitting District 2 county commissioner and board vice-chairman; qualified Republican candidate in 2026.

taxes.summary: Says Lake County's property-tax rate is the lowest in the region and he intends to keep it that way.
taxes.quote: Lake County's property tax rate is the lowest in the region, and I intend to keep it that way.

sources.title: Re-Elect Sean Parks for Lake County Commissioner

property_tax.summary: Says that as of now he would vote no on Amendment 3 unless shown it is not a 'shell game'; says he supports real tax relief but not shifting costs to fees or cutting public safety and roads.
property_tax.quote: As of today, I would vote no, unless someone can show me this is not simply a shell game before the November election.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Lake County Commission District 2 (News 6 / News Collaborative of Central Florida)

other_issues.title: Data centers
other_issues.summary: Says data centers should pay the full cost of the power and infrastructure they need ('cost-causer pays') and that he supported the county's pause on data centers; defended listening to the Lake 100 business group, which backs a conditional-use permit approach.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Lake County Commission District 2 (News 6 / News Collaborative of Central Florida)
Lake County considers tighter rules for data centers as residents call for ban (News 6)

record.item: Oct. 13, 2026: commission voted 3-2 to postpone authorizing a public hearing on draft data-center rules after Parks proposed edits the rest of the board had not reviewed, and asked staff to draft a 90-day extension of the moratorium; Campione and Sabatini were the no votes (per a Mid Florida Newspapers report summarized by Strisker).

sources.title: Data Centers: Daily Notes, October 15, 2026 (Strisker; summarizes Mid Florida Newspapers report 'Lake County delays vote on data center rules, weighs moratorium extension')
